B1 bridge, unit 10: a NEW course-authored explanatory text (local history), written to teach the lemma pack planned for an adaptation of Martí's "Historia del hombre contada por sus casas" (owner decision of 2026-10-06 (1): Gutenberg texts are not adapted; the topic, plot and wording here are original). The town, its people and the events are COMPOSITE and invented for the course; the reviewer should decide whether it needs a visible "invented local history" label. For the Honduran reviewer: (a) the register is a short local-history article written for a municipal booklet, with quoted memories; (b) "nivola" is a word coined by the writer Unamuno (here it is a word a local teacher invents; the pack asks for it): check that the aside reads naturally; (c) "señorito", "merced", "ay", "bah", "embargo" (sin embargo) and "ente" are deliberate pack items; (d) informal address in the quotations is voseo; (e) "canario" is used for a man from the Canary Islands.

sentences.text: El parque de este pueblo del norte tiene hoy cuatro bancos, un árbol viejo y cinco pinos altos.
sentences.english: The park of this northern town has four benches, an old tree and five tall pines today.

sentences.text: Pero hace cien años no era un parque: era un campo de tierra, con un solo pino y un camino largo.
sentences.english: But a hundred years ago it was not a park: it was a field of dirt, with a single pine and a long road.

sentences.text: Los vecinos cuentan que el cura plantó los primeros pinos con sus propias manos, y que era un hombre viejo, con una barba blanca y una voz muy fuerte.
sentences.english: The neighbors say that the priest planted the first pines with his own hands, and that he was an old man, with a white beard and a very strong voice.

sentences.text: «El cura de la barba blanca era bueno —dice doña Mercedes—.
sentences.english: "The priest with the white beard was good," says doña Mercedes.

sentences.text: Un día se atrevió a decirle al capitán que el campo era de todos.»
sentences.english: "One day he dared to tell the captain that the field belonged to everyone."

sentences.text: —Así fue —prosiguió—.
sentences.english: "That is how it was," she went on.

sentences.text: Y desde entonces nadie se atrevió a decir que el parque era de uno solo.
sentences.english: "And from then on nobody dared to say that the park belonged to one person alone."

sentences.text: El capitán era el jefe del pueblo, y tenía su despacho en una casa pintada de rojo, al lado del campo.
sentences.english: The captain was the head of the town, and he had his office in a house painted red, next to the field.

sentences.text: Sin embargo, no era un hombre malo, y al cabo de un año dio la orden de plantar más árboles.
sentences.english: However, he was not a bad man, and after a year he gave the order to plant more trees.

sentences.text: Así empezó el parque: con un viejo, un jefe y unos árboles que crecían despacio.
sentences.english: That is how the park began: with an old man, a chief and some trees that grew slowly.

sentences.text: Pero la existencia de un parque no es cosa de un día.
sentences.english: But the existence of a park is not the matter of a single day.

sentences.text: Al cabo de diez años, el viento llevaba las hojas por todo el camino.
sentences.english: After ten years, the wind carried the leaves all along the road.

sentences.text: Las hojas eran largas y secas, y los niños las usaban para hacer escobas pequeñas.
sentences.english: The leaves were long and dry, and the children used them to make little brooms.

sentences.text: Por suerte, había buena agua, y el campo seco se puso verde.
sentences.english: Luckily, there was good water, and the dry field turned green.

sentences.text: «Tuvimos suerte —dice doña Mercedes—.
sentences.english: "We were lucky," says doña Mercedes.

sentences.text: Con mala suerte, no habría pueblo.»
sentences.english: "With bad luck, there would be no town."

sentences.text: Al cabo de otro tiempo, esa orden se cumplió, y el parque tuvo su primera casa pintada de blanco.
sentences.english: After another while, that order was carried out, and the park had its first house painted white.

sentences.text: La segunda casa fue pintada de azul por un maestro, y en ella estuvo el despacho de la escuela.
sentences.english: The second house was painted blue by a teacher, and the school's office was in it.

sentences.text: Hoy esa casa sigue ahí, a merced del sol y de las lluvias, y la orden de cuidarla pasó de padres a hijos.
sentences.english: Today that house is still there, at the mercy of the sun and the rains, and the order to take care of it passed from parents to children.

sentences.text: Los años siguientes trajeron gente nueva.
sentences.english: The following years brought new people.

sentences.text: Primero llegó un inglés, un ingeniero que venía a hacer el tren, y se quedó dos años en una casa cerca del parque.
sentences.english: First came an Englishman, an engineer who came to build the railway, and he stayed two years in a house near the park.

sentences.text: El inglés hablaba poco español, pero observó todo con mucho cuidado, y escribió una carta larga.
sentences.english: The Englishman spoke little Spanish, but he observed everything very carefully, and he wrote a long letter.

sentences.text: «El pueblo vive a merced de la lluvia —escribió—: si llueve poco, no hay comida, y si llueve mucho, el río se lleva los caminos.»
sentences.english: "The town lives at the mercy of the rain," he wrote: "if it rains little, there is no food, and if it rains a lot, the river takes away the roads."

sentences.text: También llegó un canario, un hombre de las islas Canarias, que abrió una tienda de carne y de pan en una esquina.
sentences.english: A man from the Canary Islands also arrived, who opened a shop for meat and bread on a corner.

sentences.text: El canario vendía carne de cerdo los sábados, y la gente se reunía a comprar y a hablar.
sentences.english: The Canarian sold pork on Saturdays, and people gathered to buy and to talk.

sentences.text: Aquellas conversaciones eran la mejor manera de saber qué pasaba en el pueblo.
sentences.english: Those conversations were the best way to know what was going on in the town.

sentences.text: «Con una conversación en la tienda del canario se sabía todo —cuenta una vecina—: quién se casaba, quién estaba enfermo, quién tenía carne esa semana.»
sentences.english: "With one conversation in the Canarian's shop you knew everything," a neighbor says: "who was getting married, who was sick, who had meat that week."

sentences.text: El inglés observó que las mujeres eran las que mejor hablaban, y las que más oían.
sentences.english: The Englishman observed that the women were the ones who spoke best, and the ones who listened most.

sentences.text: Un matrimonio joven abrió después la primera farmacia, y el marido era capaz de leer cuatro idiomas.
sentences.english: A young married couple later opened the first pharmacy, and the husband was able to read four languages.

sentences.text: El hijo de ese matrimonio, capaz de todo, fue más tarde el primer médico del pueblo.
sentences.english: The son of that couple, capable of anything, was later the town's first doctor.

sentences.text: El matrimonio ayudaba a los enfermos sin pedir dinero, y la mujer era capaz de sanar con hierbas.
sentences.english: The couple helped the sick without asking for money, and the wife was able to heal with herbs.

sentences.text: Pero no todos eran tan buenos.
sentences.english: But not everybody was so good.

sentences.text: Un señorito de la ciudad llegó con un carro nuevo y quiso comprar todo el parque.
sentences.english: A young gentleman from the city arrived with a new car and wanted to buy the whole park.

sentences.text: —¿Para qué querés tanta tierra? —le preguntó el viejo de la barba.
sentences.english: "What do you want so much land for?" the old man with the beard asked him.

sentences.text: —Bah, para nada —dijo el señorito—.
sentences.english: "Bah, for nothing," said the young gentleman.

sentences.text: Para conquistar el pueblo.
sentences.english: "To conquer the town."

sentences.text: —Conquistar un pueblo es imposible, hijo —prosiguió el viejo, con calma—.
sentences.english: "To conquer a town is impossible, my son," the old man went on, calmly.

sentences.text: Un pueblo sólo se conquista cuando ya es tuyo.
sentences.english: "A town is only conquered when it is already yours."

sentences.text: —¡Bah!
sentences.english: "Bah!

sentences.text: Eso es imposible de creer —dijo el señorito.
sentences.english: That is impossible to believe," said the young gentleman.

sentences.text: Pero se fue sin decir nada, y el parque siguió siendo de todos.
sentences.english: But he left without saying anything, and the park remained everyone's.

sentences.text: —Ay, qué hombre tan malo —dijeron algunos—.
sentences.english: "Ay, what a bad man," some said.

sentences.text: Bah, ya se le pasará.
sentences.english: "Bah, he will get over it."

sentences.text: Esa tarde nadie quiso hablar más, y sólo quedó el viento.
sentences.english: That afternoon nobody wanted to talk any more, and only the wind was left.

sentences.text: En 1930 se construyó la escuela de la esquina, y con ella llegaron los primeros maestros.
sentences.english: In 1930 the school on the corner was built, and with it came the first teachers.

sentences.text: La portera de la escuela era una mujer resignada, y casi nunca hablaba.
sentences.english: The school's caretaker was a resigned woman, and she hardly ever spoke.

sentences.text: Pero guardaba en silencio todo lo que oía, y por eso los maestros le contaban sus problemas en el despacho.
sentences.english: But she kept in silence everything she heard, and that is why the teachers told her their problems in the office.

sentences.text: «La portera sabía más que todos los libros —dice un maestro viejo—.
sentences.english: "The caretaker knew more than all the books," says an old teacher.

sentences.text: Su silencio era una creación, como una canción que nadie canta.»
sentences.english: "Her silence was a creation, like a song that nobody sings."

sentences.text: Una vecina decía que ella era tan resignada que era la mujer más feliz del pueblo.
sentences.english: A neighbor said that the caretaker was so resigned that she was the happiest woman in the town.

sentences.text: Nunca la oían decir una palabra mala, y su cara resignada era una señal de paz.
sentences.english: They never heard her say a bad word, and her resigned face was a sign of peace.

sentences.text: Uno de esos maestros, don Ricardo, escribía versos por las noches, y los leía a los vecinos en el parque.
sentences.english: One of those teachers, don Ricardo, wrote verses at night, and read them to the neighbors in the park.

sentences.text: Algunos decían que sus versos eran ridículos, porque hablaban de los pinos como si fueran personas.
sentences.english: Some said his verses were ridiculous, because they spoke of the pines as if they were people.

sentences.text: Nadie quería hacer el ridículo, y por eso casi nadie los leía en voz alta.
sentences.english: Nobody wanted to look ridiculous, and that is why hardly anybody read them aloud.

sentences.text: —¡Ay, maestro! —le decían—.
sentences.english: "Ay, teacher!" they said to him.

sentences.text: ¿Quién va a querer un árbol con nombre?
sentences.english: "Who is going to want a tree with a name?"

sentences.text: Don Ricardo sonreía y prosiguió con sus versos, y un día escribió un libro grande.
sentences.english: Don Ricardo smiled and kept on with his verses, and one day he wrote a big book.

sentences.text: No era una novela ni un cuento, y el maestro le puso un nombre inventado: una nivola.
sentences.english: It was not a novel or a tale, and the teacher gave it an invented name: a nivola.

sentences.text: «Una nivola es una obra de ficción —explicaba—, pero hecha con personas de verdad: el viejo, el capitán, la portera.»
sentences.english: "A nivola is a work of fiction," he explained, "but made with real people: the old man, the captain, the caretaker."

sentences.text: El libro habla de un ente extraño, mitad árbol y mitad hombre, que cuida el parque de noche.
sentences.english: The book is about a strange being, half tree and half man, who watches over the park at night.

sentences.text: Ese ente de ficción habla con los vecinos, y casi siempre les dice lo contrario de lo que esperan.
sentences.english: That fictional being talks to the neighbors, and almost always tells them the opposite of what they expect.

sentences.text: Los niños devoraban el libro en la escuela, y una niña quiso devorar todos los libros del maestro, y los devoró en una semana.
sentences.english: The children devoured the book at school, and one girl wanted to devour all the teacher's books, and devoured them in a week.

sentences.text: Jugaban a ser él, y todos hacían lo contrario de lo que se les pedía.
sentences.english: They played at being him, and everyone did the opposite of what they were asked.

sentences.text: —Es lo contrario de la escuela —se reía el maestro.
sentences.english: "It is the opposite of school," the teacher laughed.

sentences.text: Un joven anarquista, llegado de la costa, leyó el libro con gozo.
sentences.english: A young anarchist, who had arrived from the coast, read the book with delight.

sentences.text: Dijo que el ente de don Ricardo era un anarquista también, porque no obedecía a nadie.
sentences.english: He said that don Ricardo's being was also an anarchist, because it obeyed nobody.

sentences.text: El maestro contestó que no: que un anarquista no cree en la ficción, y que su figura era sólo una creación de papel.
sentences.english: The teacher answered no: that an anarchist does not believe in fiction, and that his figure was only a creation of paper.

sentences.text: Con el tiempo, el parque tuvo también música.
sentences.english: In time, the park also had music.

sentences.text: Un pianista que tocaba en el cine se sentaba los domingos bajo los árboles, y tocaba un piano viejo que le prestaban.
sentences.english: A pianist who played at the cinema sat under the trees on Sundays, and played an old piano that they lent him.

sentences.text: El pianista no tenía casa propia, y vivía a merced de lo que le daban los vecinos.
sentences.english: The pianist had no house of his own, and lived at the mercy of what the neighbors gave him.

sentences.text: Sin embargo, su música daba tanto gozo que nadie lo dejaba solo.
sentences.english: However, his music gave so much joy that nobody left him alone.

sentences.text: Sin embargo, el pianista nunca quiso otra casa, y tocaba hasta muy tarde.
sentences.english: However, the pianist never wanted another house, and played until very late.

sentences.text: Una mujer de la ciudad, que estudiaba psicología, pasó tres semanas en el parque con un libro de psicología bajo el brazo.
sentences.english: A woman from the city, who studied psychology, spent three weeks in the park with a psychology book under her arm.

sentences.text: Escribió lo que veía, y dijo que la psicología de los pueblos pequeños era más fácil de lo que se pensaba.
sentences.english: She wrote down what she saw, and said that the psychology of small towns was easier than people thought.

sentences.text: Observó que la existencia de la gente era dura, pero que la conversación la hacía más fácil.
sentences.english: She observed that people's existence was hard, but that conversation made it easier.

sentences.text: «La necesidad nos hace hablar —escribió—, y hablar nos hace pueblo.»
sentences.english: "Need makes us talk," she wrote, "and talking makes us a town."

sentences.text: Algunos se rieron: «Ay, esa señora quiere hacernos creer que somos brutos».
sentences.english: Some laughed: "Ay, that lady wants to make us believe we are brutes."

sentences.text: Pero ella contestó con calma que los brutos no escriben versos ni inventan palabras.
sentences.english: But she answered calmly that brutes do not write verses or invent words.

sentences.text: Pensaba, además, que era imposible conocer un pueblo sin escuchar a los brutos y a los que saben por igual.
sentences.english: She also thought that it was impossible to know a town without listening to the brutes and to those who know alike.

sentences.text: Esa fue una buena respuesta, y desde entonces todos la saludaban en el parque.
sentences.english: That was a good answer, and from then on everybody greeted her in the park.

sentences.text: Hoy el parque tiene cinco árboles, un banco nuevo y una historia que nadie ha escrito del todo.
sentences.english: Today the park has five trees, a new bench and a history that nobody has written completely.

sentences.text: Doña Mercedes dice que la existencia del parque es una creación de todos los vecinos.
sentences.english: Doña Mercedes says that the existence of the park is a creation of all the neighbors.

sentences.text: Y don Ricardo, ya viejo, sigue escribiendo cada noche, con la esperanza de terminar su libro.
sentences.english: And don Ricardo, already old, keeps writing every night, in the hope of finishing his book.

sentences.text: «Cada pueblo es una nivola —dice—, una mezcla de lo que existe y de lo que se ha inventado.»
sentences.english: "Every town is a nivola," he says, "a mixture of what exists and of what has been invented."
